proposals.before: Early in Tang Qianfu he passed the jinshi; when Chief Minister Pei Tan concurrently administered the salt monopoly, he left office as a patrol official under him.
proposals.after: Early in Tang Qianfu he passed the jinshi; when Chief Minister Pei Tan concurrently administered the salt monopoly, he received his first appointment as a patrol official under him.
proposals.reason: 解褐 means taking up one's first office after the commoner gown, not leaving office; the literal English reverses the sense.

proposals.before: After mourning he resumed as Secretariat Drafter and was soon called into the Hanlin as Expositor.
proposals.after: After mourning he resumed as Secretariat Drafter and was soon called into the Hanlin as Academician Recipient of Edicts.
proposals.reason: 承旨學士 is the Hanlin academician who receives imperial oral commands, not an Expositor (侍講).

proposals.before: When mourning ended he was again made Secretariat Drafter, soon summoned to the Hanlin as Expositor.
proposals.after: When mourning ended he was again made Secretariat Drafter, soon summoned to the Hanlin as Academician Recipient of Edicts.
proposals.reason: 承旨學士 is misrendered as Expositor in the literal English as well.

proposals.before: His son Zhuo rose to Director of the Secretariat under Later Zhou in the Xiande era.
proposals.after: His son Zhuo rose to Director of the Palace Library under Later Zhou in the Xiande era.
proposals.reason: 秘書監 is the director of the palace/imperial library, not the Secretariat (中書).

proposals.before: His son Zhuo, in Later Zhou Xiande, reached Director of the Secretariat.
proposals.after: His son Zhuo, in Later Zhou Xiande, reached Director of the Palace Library.
proposals.reason: 秘書監 is mistranslated as Director of the Secretariat in the literal English.

proposals.before: He took the jinshi in Qianfu and moved through salt patrol work, Collegiate Reviser, remonstrator, palace and diarist posts, then Hanlin academician, Vice Minister of Rites and edict drafter, and Director of Merit without changing his core duties.
proposals.after: He took the jinshi in Qianfu and moved through finance patrol work, Collegiate Reviser, remonstrator, palace and diarist posts, then Hanlin academician, Vice Director of Rites and edict drafter, and Director of Merit without changing his core duties.
proposals.reason: 度支巡官 is a finance/census patrol post, not salt; 禮部員外郎 is a bureau vice-director, not Vice Minister (侍郎).

proposals.before: In Tang Qianfu he passed the jinshi and served in succession as salt patrol official, Collegiate Reviser, remonstrator, palace and diarist posts, was summoned as Hanlin academician, made Vice Minister of Rites and edict drafter, transferred to Director of Merit, his duties unchanged.
proposals.after: In Tang Qianfu he passed the jinshi and served in succession as finance patrol official, Collegiate Reviser, remonstrator, palace and diarist posts, was summoned as Hanlin academician, made Vice Director of Rites and edict drafter, transferred to Director of Merit, his duties unchanged.
proposals.reason: Same errors as the idiomatic field: 度支 is not salt, and 員外郎 is not Vice Minister.

proposals.before: He went on to serve as Vice Minister of Revenue and War and as Hanlin Expositor.
proposals.after: He went on to serve as Vice Minister of Revenue and War and as Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts.
proposals.reason: 學士承旨 is Recipient of Edicts, not Expositor.

proposals.before: He served in succession as Vice Minister of Revenue and War and as Expositor.
proposals.after: He served in succession as Vice Minister of Revenue and War and as Academician Recipient of Edicts.
proposals.reason: 學士承旨 is misrendered as Expositor.

proposals.before: As a boy Ce was quick-witted and studious, with a special love of poetry.
proposals.after: As a boy Ce was quick-witted and studious, with a special love of chapter-and-verse learning.
proposals.reason: 章句 denotes classical chapter-and-phrase exegesis, not poetry; the idiomatic rendering invents a poetic bent.

proposals.before: Ce in youth was clever and fond of learning, especially delighting in regulated verse.
proposals.after: Ce in youth was clever and fond of learning, especially delighting in chapter-and-phrase study.
proposals.reason: 章句 is textual exegesis, not regulated verse; the literal over-specifies the wrong genre.

proposals.before: When grief ended he wore a seven-foot headcloth and buried himself in obscurity for nearly ten years.
proposals.after: When grief ended he wore a seven-sheng coarse headcloth and buried himself in obscurity for nearly ten years.
proposals.reason: 幅巾七升 uses 升 as a cloth-grade measure for mourning dress, not a length of seven feet.

proposals.before: Someone said to him: "When Ji Kang of the Central Mountains died, his son Shao buried himself in obscurity and would not show himself; Shan Tao urged him by the logic of things, and only then did he take office.
proposals.after: Someone said to him: "When Zhongsan Gentleman Ji Kang died, his son Shao buried himself in obscurity and would not show himself; Shan Tao urged him by the logic of things, and only then did he take office.
proposals.reason: 嵇中散 is Ji Kang's office title 中散大夫, not a toponym 'Central Mountains'.

proposals.before: Jing Xiang, styled Zizhen, came from Fenyin in Tongzhou.
proposals.after: Jing Xiang, styled Zizhen, came from Fengyi in Tongzhou.
proposals.reason: Chinese 馮翊 is Fengyi, not Fenyin (汾陰); the native-place name is mistranslated.

proposals.before: Jing Xiang, styled Zizhen, was a native of Fenyin in Tongzhou.
proposals.after: Jing Xiang, styled Zizhen, was a native of Fengyi in Tongzhou.
proposals.reason: Chinese 馮翊 is Fengyi, not Fenyin; literal English repeats the same place-name error.

proposals.before: In the fourth month of summer, Kaiping 3, with Bin and Qi raiding, the Founder sent Liu Zhijun west against Zheng and Yan; deeply worried, he turned to Xiang at a banquet to ask about the western front.
proposals.after: In the fourth month of summer, Kaiping 3, with Bin and Qi raiding, the Founder sent Liu Zhijun west against Fu and Yan; deeply worried, he turned to Xiang at a banquet to ask about the western front.
proposals.reason: Chinese 鄜 is Fu (Fuzhou), not Zheng; 鄜、延 are Fu and Yan.

proposals.before: Kaiping year 3, fourth month of summer: the Founder because Bin and Qi were harrying sent Liu Zhijun west to attack Zheng and Yan, deeply feared failure, and at a banquet turned to Xiang to ask about western affairs.
proposals.after: Kaiping year 3, fourth month of summer: the Founder because Bin and Qi were harrying sent Liu Zhijun west to attack Fu and Yan, deeply feared failure, and at a banquet turned to Xiang to ask about western affairs.
proposals.reason: Chinese 鄜 is Fu, not Zheng; literal English mistranslates the prefecture name.

proposals.before: When the Founder was gravely ill, Xiang was summoned to the imperial bedside to receive the entrusting command; he deeply resented the Jin enemy; Xiang sobbed and could not bear it; he received the mandate and withdrew.
proposals.after: When the Founder was gravely ill, Xiang was summoned to the imperial bedside to receive the entrusting command; and he (the Founder) deeply regretted the Jin enemy; Xiang sobbed and could not bear it; he received the mandate and withdrew.
proposals.reason: In 且深以並寇為恨 the subject is the dying Founder's regret, not Xiang; literal English wrongly attributes the resentment to Xiang.

proposals.before: After Liu Xun lost Hebei and An Yan lost Yangliu, Xiang memorialized: "Year after year we send armies abroad while our borders shrink—not only are the troops arrogant and the generals timid; our strategy is wrong as well.
proposals.after: After Liu Xun lost Hebei and An Yanzhi lost Yangliu, Xiang memorialized: "Year after year we send armies abroad while our borders shrink—not only are the troops arrogant and the generals timid; our strategy is wrong as well.
proposals.reason: Chinese 安彥之 is An Yanzhi; packet English truncates the given name to Yan.

proposals.before: When Liu Xun lost Hebei, and An Yan lost Yangliu, Xiang memorialized saying: "The state year after year sends generals on campaign; the borders daily shrink—not only are troops arrogant and generals timid; disposition too has not obtained its method.
proposals.after: When Liu Xun lost Hebei, and An Yanzhi lost Yangliu, Xiang memorialized saying: "The state year after year sends generals on campaign; the borders daily shrink—not only are troops arrogant and generals timid; disposition too has not obtained its method.
proposals.reason: Chinese 安彥之 is An Yanzhi; literal English likewise truncates the name.

proposals.before: Now the enemy has reached Yanzhou while Your Majesty shows no alarm—that is what I cannot understand first.
proposals.after: Now the enemy has reached Yunzhou while Your Majesty shows no alarm—that is what I cannot understand first.
proposals.reason: Chinese 鄆州 is Yunzhou; Yanzhou misreads the toponym.

proposals.before: Now the enemy's horses have already reached Yan prefecture; Your Majesty does not keep sage concern—what I cannot understand is the first point.
proposals.after: Now the enemy's horses have already reached Yun prefecture; Your Majesty does not keep sage concern—what I cannot understand is the first point.
proposals.reason: Chinese 鄆州 is Yun prefecture; Yan prefecture is the wrong reading.

proposals.before: Li Zhen, styled Xingxu, was great-grandson of Tang's Bao Zhen, military commissioner of Lu prefecture.
proposals.after: Li Zhen, styled Xingxu, was great-grandson of Tang's Li Baozhen, military commissioner of Lu prefecture.
proposals.reason: Chinese 抱真 is Li Baozhen; literal drops the surname present in the idiomatic rendering.

proposals.before: When the Founder also held Yanzhou he made him deputy commissioner of the Tianping army.
proposals.after: When the Founder also held Yunzhou he made him deputy commissioner of the Tianping army.
proposals.reason: Chinese 鄆州 is Yunzhou; Yanzhou is incorrect.

proposals.before: When the Founder also held Yan prefecture, he appointed him deputy military commissioner of Tianping army.
proposals.after: When the Founder also held Yun prefecture, he appointed him deputy military commissioner of Tianping army.
proposals.reason: Chinese 鄆州 is Yun prefecture; Yan prefecture misreads the toponym.

proposals.before: At Tong Pass the court had already offered congratulations to the new regime.
proposals.after: When Zhen reached Shaan, Shaan had already offered congratulations.
proposals.reason: Chinese 陝 denotes Shaan; the idiomatic line invents Tong Pass and adds 'the court/new regime' not present in the source.

proposals.before: Military inspector Liu Chongchu, Jishu's brother, and former chancellor Zhang Jun at Gou in Henan also urged the Founder: "Side with the eunuchs and all goes easily—you get what you want."
proposals.after: Military inspector Liu Chongchu, Jishu's elder brother, and former chancellor Zhang Jun lodging at Gou in Henan also urged the Founder: "Side with the eunuchs and all goes easily—you get what you want."
proposals.reason: Chinese 兄 marks elder brother; the idiomatic gloss drops that seniority, which the literal preserves.

proposals.before: At Qingzhou Shifan left headquarters the same day and gave Zhen the military and surveillance seals, records, and keys.
proposals.after: At Qingzhou, Shifan left headquarters the same day and gave Zhen the military and surveillance seals, records, and keys.
proposals.reason: Missing comma fuses place Qingzhou with personal name Shifan into a false reading Qingzhou Shifan.

proposals.before: At the end of Han, Xiu had often fought Cao Cao—was that loyalty? When Yuan Shao tried to win him, Jia Xu said: 'The Yuans cannot even tolerate each other—how could they lead the realm? Cao Cao holds the Son of Heaven and commands the lords; his aim is great and he does not settle private scores—you should not doubt him.'
proposals.after: At the end of Han, Xiu had often fought Lord Cao—would Cao have treated that as a kindness? When Yuan Shao sent envoys to recruit Xiu, Jia Xu said: 'The Yuan father and son cannot abide each other—how could they lead the realm's heroes? Lord Cao holds the Son of Heaven and commands the feudal lords; his aim is great and he does not settle private scores—you should not doubt him.'
proposals.reason: 豈德之耶 asks whether Cao would count prior enmity as kindness owed, not Xiu's loyalty; also softens 袁家父子 and 英士.

proposals.before: In Tianyou the Tang chancellor Liu Can, courting the Founder, had seven ministers including Pei Shu and Lu Yi killed at Baima post in Huazhou.
proposals.after: In Tianyou the Tang chancellor Liu Can, courting the Founder, slandered to death seven ministers including Pei Shu and Lu Yi at Baima post in Huazhou.
proposals.reason: Chinese 譖殺 is death by slanderous denunciation; idiomatic omits the slander means.

proposals.before: When Yougui seized the throne he replaced Jing Xiang as Chongzheng Court commissioner.
proposals.after: When Yougui seized the throne, Zhen replaced Jing Xiang as Chongzheng Court commissioner.
proposals.reason: Chinese silent subject of 代敬翔為崇政院使 is Li Zhen continuing the biography; English he wrongly attributes the replacement to Yougui.

proposals.before: When commoner Yougui usurped the throne, he replaced Jing Xiang as Chongzheng Court commissioner.
proposals.after: When commoner Yougui usurped the throne, [Zhen] replaced Jing Xiang as Chongzheng Court commissioner.
proposals.reason: Literal he likewise misassigns the silent subject; the office change is Zhen succeeding Jing Xiang under Yougui usurpation.

proposals.before: The historian writes: Zhang Wenyu and Xue Yiju were old Tang ministers; when Liang forced the abdication they came as envoys and calmly handed over the throne—in such a time even a loyal minister is unlucky.
proposals.after: The historian writes: Zhang Wenyu and Xue Yiju were old Tang ministers; when Liang forced the abdication they came as envoys and casually handed over the throne—in such a time even a loyal minister is unlucky.
proposals.reason: Chinese 狎神器 implies treating the sacred vessel lightly or irreverently, not calm composure; 'casually' better matches 狎.

decisions.reason: s0004 has 解褐署巡官; 解褐 means taking first office after the commoner gown, so 'left office' reverses the Chinese and the proposed first-appointment wording is accurate.
s0010 has 承旨學士; that Hanlin post receives imperial oral commands and is not 侍講/Expositor, so the proposed title is the supported correction.
The same 承旨學士 in s0010 is misrendered as Expositor in the literal field; Academician Recipient of Edicts restores the office.
s0028 has 秘書監; that is director of the palace/imperial library, not the Secretariat (中書), so the proposed idiomatic title is correct.
The literal likewise turns 秘書監 into Director of the Secretariat; Director of the Palace Library matches the Chinese.
s0032 has 度支巡官 and 禮部員外郎; 度支 is finance/census not salt, and 員外郎 is a bureau vice-director not 侍郎, so both proposed fixes are required.
The literal repeats the same 度支/員外郎 errors; finance patrol official and Vice Director of Rites restore the Chinese offices.
s0035 has 學士承旨; that is Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts, not Expositor, and the rest of the proposed sentence is accurate.
The literal's bare 'Expositor' for 學士承旨 is the same office error; Academician Recipient of Edicts is the supported rendering.
s0048 has 尤樂章句; 章句 is classical chapter-and-phrase exegesis, so 'poetry' invents a bent the Chinese does not state.
The literal's 'regulated verse' likewise misreads 章句; chapter-and-phrase study matches the Chinese sense.
s0079 has 幅巾七升; 升 is a cloth-grade measure for mourning dress, not a length of seven feet, so the proposed wording is correct.
s0082 has 嵇中散; 中散 is the office title 中散大夫, not a toponym 'Central Mountains', so Zhongsan Gentleman is the right repair.
s0103 has 同州馮翊人; 馮翊 is Fengyi, not Fenyin (汾陰), so the proposed native-place correction is required.
The literal repeats Fenyin for 馮翊; Fengyi in Tongzhou restores the place name.
s0126 has 西討鄜、延; 鄜 is Fu (Fuzhou), not Zheng, so Fu and Yan is the supported toponym pair.
The literal's Zheng and Yan likewise misreads 鄜、延; Fu and Yan matches the Chinese prefectures.
In s0136 the 且深以並寇為恨 clause continues the Founder's deathbed charge; attributing that regret to Xiang invents the wrong subject.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 召至御床前受顧托之命，且深以並寇為恨

decisions.reason: s0140 names 安彥之; the truncated English An Yan drops the given name, and An Yanzhi restores it without other change.
The literal likewise truncates 安彥之 to An Yan; An Yanzhi is the complete name supported by the Chinese.
s0143 has 鄆州; that is Yunzhou, not Yanzhou (兗州), so the proposed toponym is correct.
The literal's Yan prefecture misreads the same 鄆州; Yun prefecture is the supported reading.
s0187 has 抱真之曾孫 in Li Zhen's biography; the ancestor is Li Baozhen, and supplying the surname Li matches the idiomatic and the historical identification.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 唐潞州節度使抱真之曾孫也

decisions.reason: s0191 has 太祖兼領鄆州; 鄆州 is Yunzhou, not Yanzhou, so the proposed idiomatic place name is required.
The literal's Yan prefecture misreads the same 鄆州; Yun prefecture restores the toponym.
s0199 is 振至陝，陝已賀矣; 陝 is Shaan, and the before text invents Tong Pass plus court/new-regime wording absent from the Chinese.
s0205 has 季述兄也 and 寓於河南緱氏; 兄 marks elder brother and 寓 marks lodging, so restoring both is a real content fix, not mere style.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 季述兄也…寓於河南緱氏

decisions.reason: s0212 separates 青州 from 師範 (振至青州，師範即日…); without the comma English can fuse place and person into a false name.
s0214's 豈德之耶 asks whether Cao would treat prior enmity as kindness owed, not whether Xiu showed loyalty; the proposed reading also restores 袁家父子 and 英士.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 繡屢與曹公立敵，豈德之耶

decisions.reason: s0221 has 譖殺; that is death by slanderous denunciation, so omitting the slander means loses Chinese content the proposed wording restores.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 譖殺大臣裴樞、陸扆等七人

decisions.reason: In Li Zhen's biography the silent subject of 代敬翔為崇政院使 is Zhen; English 'he' wrongly makes Yougui the one who takes Jing Xiang's post.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 庶人友珪篡立，代敬翔為崇政院使

decisions.after: When commoner Yougui usurped the throne, Zhen replaced Jing Xiang as Chongzheng Court commissioner.
decisions.reason: The silent subject of 代敬翔 is Zhen, so the proposed fix is right in substance, but bracketed [Zhen] is awkward in finished literal English; use plain Zhen.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 庶人友珪篡立，代敬翔為崇政院使

decisions.reason: s0229 has 狎神器以授之; 狎 marks treating the sacred vessel lightly or familiarly, so 'casually' fits and 'calmly' misreads the verb.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0019 shows the English personal name An Yan was created by truncating 安彥之; the claim must use An Yanzhi while keeping zh, pinyin, and evidence.
